extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing extensions of time, response content and form, service, and entry/acceptance of submissions in U.S. ex parte reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-month extension filing with appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner only specifies a one-month extension in its request, the patent owner must file, in addition to an appeal brief, the written request for the extension and the required fee within three months from the date of the appeal. The request and fee may be filed with or without the brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See subsection V.C. above for examples. Mere late filing beyond specified period will not effect the extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions over two months require sufficient cause and reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for any extension of time in third party requested reexaminations, and requests for an extension of more than two months from the time period set in the Office action in patent owner requested or Director ordered reexaminations, must include a showing of sufficient cause, and the extension must be for a reasonable time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation must balance patent owner's fair opportunity to respond against statutory requirement that reexamination be conducted with 'special dispatch' (35 U.S.C. 305). Such requests are only granted in extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient cause showing content
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for an extension of time (except the 'no cause' two-month extension) must fully state the reasons therefor, including what action the patent owner has taken to provide a response as of the request date and why additional time is needed despite those actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement must include a factual accounting of reasonably diligent behavior by all those responsible for preparing a response. Lack of such factual accounting weighs against granting.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-cause two-month extension in patent owner/Director-ordered reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: In patent owner requested and Director ordered reexaminations, the patent owner has the opportunity to obtain an extension of time for up to two months from the time period set in the Office action without a showing of sufficient cause ('no cause' extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for more than two months in these reexaminations are expected to be rare and only in extraordinary situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party requested reexamination first extension practice
rubrics_metrics.description: In third party requested ex parte reexaminations, a first request for an extension will generally be granted if sufficient cause is shown, and typically for a reasonable time specified—usually one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second or subsequent requests and requests for more than one month will only be granted in extraordinary situations. Reasons will be evaluated by CRU, SPRS, or TC Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirements for extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for an extension must specify the requested period of extension and be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For third-party requested reexamination, the request must be filed on or before the due date and mere filing does not effect the extension. For patent owner/Director-ordered reexamination, up-to-two-month requests must be filed no later than two months from expiration of the time period set in the Office action; requests for more than two months must be filed on or before the day action is due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions cannot exceed statutory maximums
rubrics_metrics.description: The reply or other action must be filed prior to the expiration of the period of extension, but under no situation may a reply or other action be filed later than the maximum time period set by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners and practitioners must be mindful of statute-set maximums; extensions cannot override statutory caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension to file petition from denial of reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an extension of the time period to file a petition from the denial of a request for reexamination can only be entertained by filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 with the appropriate fee to waive the time provisions of 37 CFR 1.515(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reexamination is essentially ex parte, such extension petitions (especially in third-party requested reexams) will be granted only in extraordinary situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic two-month extension upon timely first response after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a timely first response to a final rejection with a shortened statutory period is construed as including a request to extend the shortened period by an additional two months, but in no case may the period exceed six months from the date of the final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to the first response after final only, even if the response is informal and/or not signed; does not apply once notice of appeal has been filed. Objective is to avoid appeal merely to gain time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Office action extension when advisory cannot be mailed in time
rubrics_metrics.description: If the advisory action cannot be mailed in sufficient time for the patent owner to consider examiner’s position and act before termination, the examiner should grant additional time and state it in the advisory Office action (PTOL-467), inserting integer months (2–6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fractional months should not be indicated. In no case can the period for response exceed six months from mailing of final rejection. An appropriate response must be filed within the extended period; amendments must place proceeding in condition for allowance or prosecution may be terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file timely and appropriate response terminates prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action (or required interview statement), the prosecution in the ex parte reexamination proceeding will be a terminated prosecution and the Director will proceed to issue and publish a reexamination certificate under § 1.570 in accordance with the last action of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under § 1.137 may be filed to revive if the delay was unintentional (see § 1.137 and § 1.137 to revive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements for filings in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of a request for ex parte reexamination by a third party requester, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third party requester must be served on the other party in the manner provided by § 1.248; the document must reflect service or the document may be refused consideration by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent owner is required to serve a copy of any response made in the reexamination proceeding on the third party requester (37 CFR 1.550(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Active participation of third-party requester ends after reply
rubrics_metrics.description: The active participation of the ex parte reexamination requester ends with the reply pursuant to § 1.535, and no further submissions on behalf of the reexamination requester will be acknowledged or considered, except as permitted by § 1.510 or § 1.535 or if entered in the patent file prior to the date of the order for ex parte reexamination pursuant to § 1.525.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions by third parties filed after the date of the order must meet § 1.501(a) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies entry conditions (37 CFR 1.111(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply that is limited to cancellation of claim(s); adoption of examiner suggestion(s); placement of the application/proceeding in condition for allowance; reply to an Office requirement made after the first reply was filed; correction of informalities; or simplification of issues for appeal, may be entered at the examiner's discretion. It will be entered if filed during a period when Office action is suspended under § 1.103(a) or (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may approve entry after a cursory review; supplemental replies not meeting these limits will not be entered as of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and substance of a proper reply (37 CFR 1.111(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: To be entitled to reconsideration or further examination, a reply must be in writing, distinctly and specifically point out the supposed errors in the examiner’s action, reply to every ground of objection and rejection, and present arguments pointing out the specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over applied references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must appear to be a bona fide attempt to advance the application or reexamination proceeding. General allegations that claims are patentable without specifics do not comply. When amending, the applicant/patent owner must clearly point out the patentable novelty and how amendments avoid references/objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not fully responsive submission definition and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner submission is 'not fully responsive' to a non-final Office action when (A) a bona fide response is filed, (B) before expiration of the permissible response period (including extensions), and (C) through oversight or inadvertence some point necessary to a full response is omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If (A)-(C) met, prosecution should not be terminated; examiner may (A) waive non-serious deficiencies and act on submission, (B) accept amendment but issue new Office action identifying omitted part and new time, or (C) notify patent owner to complete within remaining time to avoid termination. Use practice analogous to 37 CFR 1.135(c). Form paragraph 22.14 may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling inadvertent omissions before final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When an omission is inadvertent and sufficient time remains, the examiner may telephone the patent owner and require completion within remaining period; an interview summary record must be completed. The practice does not apply where omission was deliberate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice authorizes but does not require the examiner to give a new time period. Examiners should not follow the practice if they conclude the patent owner is attempting to abuse it to obtain more time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of omissions after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: After final rejection, if a bona fide response is filed but omits some point, the examiner should not issue a notice of failure to fully respond; instead, an advisory Office action (form PTOL-467) should be issued explaining the omission. The final rejection time period continues to run and is extended by two months if the response is the first response after final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after final are entered only if they place the proceeding in condition for issuance of a reexamination certificate or are in better form for appeal; otherwise they are denied entry. If an amendment does not place the proceeding in condition for allowance, prosecution continues to run until an appropriate response (notice of appeal or qualifying amendment) is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner authority when time expired but amendment nearly places proceeding in condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Where time has expired for response and the amendment submitted would place the proceeding in condition for issuance of a reexamination certificate except for an omission through apparent oversight or inadvertence, the examiner has authority to enter the response, withdraw the final Office action, and issue a new Office action (e.g., Ex parte Quayle practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should recognize that substantial patent rights are at issue and use discretion; this course is within examiner's authority and often appropriate to avoid immediate termination where correction is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective (informal) submission grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission can be defective (informal) even if substance is complete. Examples of defects include: (A) paper lacks proof of service; (B) unsigned paper; (C) signed by non-practitioner not of record; (D) amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j); (E) amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) or (c)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use forms PTOL-475 (third-party requested reexams) or PTO-2311 (patent owner requested/Director-ordered) to notify defects, set time for correction, and explain defects. If defects not corrected, submission will not be entered and prosecution may be terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of defects and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: A time period from the mailing date of the defect notice will be set for correction of defect(s). Extension of time to correct the defect(s) may be requested under 37 CFR 1.550(c). If not corrected after notice, submission will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If failure to comply with the notice results in failure to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action, prosecution of the reexamination generally will be terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective response after final — advisory action procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a defective (informal) response is filed after final rejection (before expiration of permissible response period), the examiner should issue an advisory Office action (PTOL-467 or PTOL-467A) explaining the defect rather than PTOL-475/PTO-2311. The final rejection period continues to run and is extended by two months if the response is the first response after final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2265 and 2272 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service certification required in reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reexamination (filed by a person other than the patent owner) must include a certification that a copy of the request has been served in its entirety on the patent owner at the address provided in § 1.33(c), indicating the name and address of the party served; if service was not possible, a duplicate copy must be supplied to the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory checklist item in the reexamination request per 37 CFR 1.510 and MPEP § 2266.03.
